nodes.name: Pyrolysis transformation
nodes.procedure: NWs@polymer underwent well-controlled pyrolysis treatment at 900°C under Ar atmosphere. After pyrolysis, the NWs encapsulated in polymer are no longer visible. The position originally occupied by the NWs became a one-dimensional hollow channel, which is also free of nanoparticles. Co atoms are atomized at high temperature, causing the breakage of Co-Co bonds while the released Co atoms were then captured by the N-doped carbon support.

nodes.name: Polymer encapsulation
nodes.procedure: The prepared Co(OH)_x NWs were encapsulated in a polymer. The TEM image revealed that the prepared NWs@polymer retain the nanowire-like morphology, with the Co(OH)_x NWs encapsulated in the polymer.
nodes.source_text: The TEM image revealed that the prepared NWs@polymer retain the nanowire-like morphology, with the Co(OH)_x NWs encapsulated in the polymer (Fig. 1c, Fig. S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows uniform nanowire-like morphology of Co(OH)x NWs with average diameter 3 nm and length several micrometers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of Co(OH)x shows that the as-synthesized sample displays an uniform nanowire-like morphology with an average diameter and length of 3 nm and several micrometers, respectively (Fig. 1b, Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: No obvious diffraction peaks observed for Co(OH)x NWs due to low crystallinity; Co SACs/NC shows only broad graphitic carbon peaks at 26° and 43° with absence of cobalt peaks indicating atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, no obvious diffraction peaks can be observed in the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern for the NWs, which may due to the low crystallinity of the NWs (Fig. S2). ... The XRD patterns of the Co SACs/NC and NC display two broad peaks at around 26° and 43°, corresponding to the (002) and (101) planes, respectively, of graphitic carbon.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p XPS of Co(OH)x NWs shows peaks at 797.1 eV (Co 2p1/2), 781.2 eV (Co 2p3/2), satellites at 803.0 eV and 786.5 eV confirming cobalt hydroxide; N 1s XPS of Co SACs/NC shows pyridinic (398.5 eV), pyrrolic (400.7 eV), graphitic (401.1 eV) N species as anchoring sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum of Co 2p displays two main peaks at 797.1 and 781.2 eV, corresponding to Co 2p1/2 and 2p3/2, respectively. Moreover, two satellite peaks, located at 803.0 and 786.5 eV, respectively, can be observed. These results agree well with the characteristic XPS spectrum of Co 2p in Co(OH)x, confirming that the obtained NWs are cobalt hydroxide (Fig. S3). The high-resolution N 1s XPS spectrum revealed the coexistence of graphitic (401.1 eV), pyrrolic (400.7 eV), and pyridinic (398.5 eV) nitrogen species, which acted as anchoring sites for Co atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows large amounts of bright dots assigned to isolated Co single atoms on N-doped carbon support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1f and Fig. S7, large amounts of bright dots are observed on the entire support, which are assigned to the Co atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows Co atoms uniformly distributed on N-doped carbon support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy mapping showed that the Co atoms are uniformly distributed on the N-doped carbon support (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co content in Co SACs/NC catalyst is 0.4 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co content in the catalyst is 0.4% based on the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES absorption edge between Co foil and CoO (valence +0 to +2); EXAFS FT peak at 1.4 Å (Co-N, no Co-Co); WT max at 3.8 Å⁻¹ (Co-N); fitting shows Co coordinated by 4 N atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a illustrates the X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) curves of Co K-edge for the Co SACs/NC. The absorption edge position of Co SACs/NC is located between those of Co foil and CoO... As shown in Fig. 2b, the Fourier transform (FT) k³-weighted of the EXAFS curve for Co SACs/NC displays one main peak at about 1.4 Å, corresponding to the first coordination shell of Co-N. The absence of Co-Co bonds... Fig. 2d and e show the fitting results of Co SACs/NC, based on which the Co is coordinated with four N (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ ETEM under N2 shows Co(OH)x NWs stable up to 700°C, breaking at 800°C, and complete disappearance at 900-1000°C leaving hollow channels.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Under the temperature in the range of 500-700°C (Fig. 3b, c), the nanowire is still clearly visible. When the temperature rises to 800°C (Fig. 3d), the nanowire begins to break and disappears.
